- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce subsequent days’ forecast by 5–15% to correct for overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 10+ days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 2–5% from next 3–5 days).  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >3σ from recent 7-day mean, adjust toward historical mean to avoid mean reversion miss.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast starts high and true outcome drops below 70% of forecast within 5 days, reduce forecast slope to reflect downward momentum.
